title: Choose the drawn Dobok homepage
question: Five directions. Flip a card for the phone layout. Click the image to zoom.

options.label: Collar Frame
options.thesis: The page is a dobok V-neck: black collar tape is architecture, the three students live in the clearing, gold stitch is the only ornament.
options.viewport: Desktop: full-bleed trio inside a drawn V that grows in from the page edges. Phone: the same V, flowing off the left and right sides of the screen.
options.risk: Collar can read as a decorative border if it does not actually structure the scroll.

options.label: Unfolded Uniform
options.thesis: A diagonal cut: the photo is one field, hero type is the other. The garment is the split, not a frame around a picture.
options.viewport: Desktop: photo takes one half on a diagonal cut; hero type sits on the other half. Phone: the same split, naturally stacked.
options.risk: If the photo gets a box around it, the idea dies.

options.label: Collar V
options.thesis: The dobok V drops from the top: collar, then a small square at the point, then the school speaks.
options.viewport: Desktop: the locked V-down layout. Phone: header above (logo, name, menu), a smaller V, square at the point, headline underneath.
options.risk: The V can become a logo instead of architecture if it is too small or too ornate.

options.label: Belt Horizon
options.thesis: One red rank-tape is the horizon: the dojang is the sky, the words are the ground.
options.viewport: Desktop: full-bleed trio as a wide band above a single red tape; type below on ivory. Phone: the same stack, tape as a slim horizon, no V, no diagonal garment.
options.risk: A horizontal band can read as a generic sports site if the tape is just a red line.

options.label: Studio White
options.thesis: Gallery quiet: huge type, one hard red bar, the students as a sharp crop in white space. No stitch costume.
options.viewport: Desktop: vast white, oversized “Washougal trains here.” overlapping a sharp trio crop, hairline nav, one red rank-bar CTA. Phone: the same hierarchy, stacked, still airy.
options.risk: Can feel like a fashion lookbook instead of a family school if the photo is treated as a product.
